title: Structural Properties: Parity, Divisibility, and the Product Formula
description: Structural properties of Euler's totient function: parity (phi(n) even for n >= 3), prime characterization (phi(n) = n-1 iff n prime), divisibility (a | b implies phi(a) | phi(b)), super-multiplicativity, the product formula phi(n) = n prod(1 - 1/p), and the GCD-totient identity.

meta.assumptions: 0 axioms, 0 sorries. All results derived from Mathlib's Nat.totient API: totient_even, totient_eq_iff_prime, totient_dvd_of_dvd, totient_super_multiplicative, totient_eq_mul_prod_factors, totient_gcd_mul_totient_mul.
meta.author: Lean Genius Research Agent (formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib)

overview.historicalContext: Euler's totient function $\varphi(n)$ counts the integers in $\{1, \ldots, n\}$ coprime to $n$. Beyond its role in Euler's theorem ($a^{\varphi(n)} \equiv 1$), $\varphi$ possesses rich structural properties that connect number theory, group theory, and combinatorics. The parity result ($\varphi(n)$ is even for $n \geq 3$) follows from the involution $a \mapsto n - a$ on $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^*$, which has no fixed points when $n > 2$. The prime characterization ($\varphi(n) = n - 1 \Leftrightarrow n$ is prime) is immediate from the definition but reveals that $\varphi$ encodes primality. The product formula $\varphi(n) = n \prod_{p \mid n}(1 - 1/p)$ was known to Euler and follows from multiplicativity and the prime power formula. The GCD-totient identity $\varphi(\gcd(a,b)) \cdot \varphi(ab) = \varphi(a) \cdot \varphi(b) \cdot \gcd(a,b)$ unifies multiplicativity (coprime case) and divisibility (one divides the other) into a single formula.
overview.problemStatement: Prove the following structural properties of Euler's totient function: (1) $\varphi(n)$ is even for all $n \geq 3$; (2) $\varphi(n) = n - 1$ if and only if $n$ is prime; (3) if $a \mid b$ then $\varphi(a) \mid \varphi(b)$; (4) $\varphi(a) \cdot \varphi(b) \leq \varphi(ab)$ (super-multiplicativity); (5) $\varphi(n) = n \prod_{p \mid n}(1 - 1/p)$ (Euler's product formula); (6) $\varphi(\gcd(a,b)) \cdot \varphi(ab) = \varphi(a) \cdot \varphi(b) \cdot \gcd(a,b)$ (GCD-totient identity).
overview.proofStrategy: Each result is proved using the corresponding Mathlib lemma. The parity theorem `Nat.totient_even` uses the fixed-point-free involution argument. The prime characterization `Nat.totient_eq_iff_prime` encodes that {1,...,n-1} are all coprime to n iff n is prime. Divisibility `Nat.totient_dvd_of_dvd` follows from the surjection of unit groups induced by the canonical map Z/bZ -> Z/aZ. Super-multiplicativity and the GCD identity both follow from the factorization of the CRT kernel.
keyInsights: The parity of $\varphi(n)$ has a clean group-theoretic proof: the map $a \mapsto -a$ on $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^*$ is a fixed-point-free involution for $n > 2$ (since $a = -a$ implies $2a \equiv 0$, which forces $n \mid 2a$, impossible when $n > 2$ and $\gcd(a,n) = 1$). Every element pairs with a distinct partner, so $|(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^*| = \varphi(n)$ is even.

The prime characterization $\varphi(n) = n-1 \Leftrightarrow n$ is prime can be seen as a 'primality test via group order': $|(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^*| = n-1$ means every nonzero element is a unit, which is equivalent to $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ being a field, which is equivalent to $n$ being prime.

The divisibility $a \mid b \Rightarrow \varphi(a) \mid \varphi(b)$ follows from the surjective ring homomorphism $\mathbb{Z}/b\mathbb{Z} \twoheadrightarrow \mathbb{Z}/a\mathbb{Z}$, which restricts to a surjective group homomorphism on units. By the first isomorphism theorem, $|(\mathbb{Z}/b\mathbb{Z})^*| = |\ker| \cdot |(\mathbb{Z}/a\mathbb{Z})^*|$, giving $\varphi(a) \mid \varphi(b)$.

Super-multiplicativity $\varphi(a)\varphi(b) \leq \varphi(ab)$ strengthens to equality when $\gcd(a,b) = 1$ (multiplicativity via CRT). The GCD-totient identity quantifies the exact gap: the factor $\varphi(\gcd(a,b))/\gcd(a,b)$ measures how the overlap in prime factors inflates the totient of the product.

Euler's product formula $\varphi(n) = n \prod_{p \mid n}(1 - 1/p)$ connects the totient to analytic number theory: the density of integers coprime to $n$ in $\{1, \ldots, N\}$ approaches $\varphi(n)/n = \prod_{p \mid n}(1 - 1/p)$. This 'inclusion-exclusion over primes' is the arithmetic analogue of a sieve.

sections.title: Part I: Parity of Totient Values
sections.summary: Proves phi(n) is even for n >= 3, characterizes odd totient (n in {1,2}), and shows phi(n) = 1 iff n in {1,2}.

sections.title: Part II: The Prime Characterization
sections.summary: Proves phi(p) = p-1 iff p is prime (for p > 0), phi(n) < n for n > 1, phi(n) <= n, and phi(n) > 0 iff n > 0.

sections.title: Part III: Divisibility Properties
sections.summary: Proves a | b implies phi(a) | phi(b), super-multiplicativity phi(a)*phi(b) <= phi(ab), and totient formulas for prime multiples.

sections.title: Part IV: Euler's Product Formula
sections.summary: Three equivalent forms of the product formula: rational form phi(n) = n * prod(1-1/p), factorization form, and division form.

sections.title: Part V: The GCD-Totient Identity
sections.summary: The identity phi(gcd(a,b)) * phi(ab) = phi(a) * phi(b) * gcd(a,b), unifying multiplicativity and divisibility.

sections.title: Part VI: Concrete Verifications
sections.summary: Verified examples: parity checks, prime characterization examples, super-multiplicativity strict inequality, divisibility instance, GCD identity computation, product formula check.

conclusion.summary: Sixteen structural properties of Euler's totient function are formalized, spanning parity, prime characterization, divisibility, super-multiplicativity, the product formula, and the GCD-totient identity. All proofs are verified with 0 axioms and 0 sorries, derived from Mathlib's comprehensive Nat.totient API.
conclusion.implications: These structural properties are foundational for applications of the totient function: the prime characterization underlies Miller-Rabin and similar primality tests; the product formula is essential for sieve methods and average-order estimates; the GCD-totient identity appears in the study of multiplicative functions on lattices. The parity result constrains the range of phi and is used in proofs about primitive roots.
openQuestions: Can the range of phi be characterized more precisely? Specifically, which even numbers appear as values of phi(n)? (This is related to Carmichael's conjecture: every value phi(n) is taken at least twice.)
Is there a Lean proof that phi(n) >= sqrt(n) for all n > 6? This would require bounding the product formula from below using prime number estimates.
Can the super-multiplicativity inequality be sharpened to phi(a)*phi(b)*gcd(a,b)/phi(gcd(a,b)) = phi(ab), giving exact equality via the GCD-totient identity?

crossReferences.description: Base theorem a^phi(n) = 1 (mod n). This entry explores structural properties of phi itself.
Multiplicativity phi(mn) = phi(m)*phi(n) for coprime m,n. This entry adds super-multiplicativity and the GCD identity as generalizations.
Divisor sum identity n = sum phi(d). The product formula here gives an alternative computation of phi via prime factors.
Carmichael's function lambda(n). The parity result phi(n) even (n >= 3) implies lambda(n) is even too (since lambda | phi).
